Stripe Id.description: Unique identifier for each stripe, such as stripe_0001.

Reference.description: Literature or author from which the data originate, such as Vian et al.

Species.description: Species to which the sample belongs, usually human or mouse.

Genome Build.description: Genome build version used for genomic coordinates, such as hg38, hg19, or mm10.

Biosample.description: Biological sample type used in the experiment, such as a cell line or tissue type (e.g. GM12878, a human B lymphocyte cell line).

Assay.description: Experimental assay type, usually Hi-C or Micro-C, which are techniques used to study chromosome conformation.

Accession.description: Accession number of the dataset in a public database (such as GEO or 4DN), for example GSE63525.

Resolution Bp.description: Resolution used for data extraction, in base pairs; for example, 10000 means each bin is 10 kb.

Normalization.description: Normalization method applied to the data, such as ICE, KR, OE, or raw (not normalized).

Chrom.description: Chromosome on which the stripe data are located (e.g. chr15).

Stripe Region.description: Genomic coordinate region covered by the stripe. It consists of two parts: the first region represents the width of the stripe, and the second region represents the length of the stripe, for example Chr15:25310001-25370000 Chr15:24490001-25370000.

Patch Matrix Size.description: Dimension of the patch interaction matrix associated with the stripe (e.g. 215 × 215).

Patch Genomic Span.description: Total genomic length covered by the patch matrix (e.g. 2.14MB), representing the length of the Patch Region.

Patch Region.description: Specific genomic coordinate range corresponding to the patch matrix (e.g. Chr15:23790000-25930000).

Patch Path.description: File path where the patch interaction matrix data are stored.
